items.followUp: A bus slows uniformly from 25 m s⁻¹ to 10 m s⁻¹ in 3 s. Find its retardation.

rubric.why: These are the initial velocity, final velocity and time given in the question, expressed in SI units.
rubric.how: Award for correctly writing u = 30 m s⁻¹, v = 15 m s⁻¹ and t = 5 s.

rubric.why: Acceleration is the change in velocity divided by the time taken.
rubric.how: Award for writing a = (v − u)/t or an equivalent formula.

rubric.why: The final and initial velocities are substituted in the correct order, along with the time.
rubric.how: Award for correctly substituting v = 15 m s⁻¹, u = 30 m s⁻¹ and t = 5 s.

rubric.why: The calculation gives a negative acceleration, indicating that the car is slowing down.
rubric.how: Award for obtaining a = −3 m s⁻².

rubric.why: Retardation is the magnitude of the negative acceleration.
rubric.description: States the retardation with its unit.
rubric.how: Award for giving retardation as 3 m s⁻².

modelAnswer: Given: u = 30 m s⁻¹, v = 15 m s⁻¹, t = 5 s.
Substitution: a = (15 m s⁻¹ − 30 m s⁻¹)/(5 s).
Retardation = magnitude of a = 3 m s⁻².

items.followUp: A steering wheel has a radius of 20 cm. Find the torque produced by a couple of 40 N.

rubric.why: The force and radius are identified, and the radius is converted to metres.
rubric.description: Writes the given data in SI units.
rubric.how: Award for identifying F = 50 N and r = 16 cm = 0.16 m.

rubric.why: The perpendicular distance between the forces acting on opposite sides of the wheel is its diameter.
rubric.description: Finds the arm of the couple.
rubric.how: Award for finding the couple arm as 2r = 0.32 m.

rubric.why: The torque of a couple is the force multiplied by the perpendicular distance between the forces.
rubric.how: Award for using torque = force × couple arm.

rubric.why: The force is multiplied by the calculated arm of the couple.
rubric.how: Award for substituting 50 N and 0.32 m into the formula.

rubric.why: The product gives the torque in newton metres.
rubric.description: States the final torque with its unit.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 50 N, r = 16 cm = 0.16 m.
The couple arm is the diameter of the steering wheel: d = 2r = 2 × 0.16 m = 0.32 m.
Formula: torque of a couple = Fd.

items.followUp: A square plate has a side of 5 mm. Find the pressure on it when a force of 10 N acts normally on it.

rubric.why: The force and side length are identified, and the side length is converted to metres.
rubric.description: Writes the given data in SI units.
rubric.how: Award for identifying F = 20 N and side = 10 mm = 0.01 m.

rubric.why: The area of the square is the square of its side length.
rubric.description: Calculates the area of the square head.

rubric.why: Pressure is force per unit area.
The given force and calculated area are substituted into the pressure formula.
rubric.how: Award for substituting 20 N and 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ m².

rubric.why: Dividing force by area gives pressure in pascals.
rubric.description: States the final pressure with its unit.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 20 N, side = 10 mm = 0.01 m.
Area of the square head: A = side² = (0.01 m)² = 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ m².

items.followUp: Define atomic physics and particle physics.

rubric.why: Plasma physics studies plasma, which is an ionized state of matter.
rubric.how: Award for stating that plasma physics studies plasma or ionized matter.

accept: structure and properties of atomic nuclei
rubric.why: Nuclear physics studies atomic nuclei, including their structure and properties.
rubric.how: Award for stating that nuclear physics studies atomic nuclei or their structure and properties.

modelAnswer: Plasma physics is the branch of physics that studies plasma, an ionized state of matter.
Nuclear physics is the branch of physics that studies the structure and properties of atomic nuclei.

items.followUp: Give two reasons why scientists use standard units of measurement.

rubric.why: SI units provide a shared standard of measurement for scientists internationally.
rubric.description: States that SI units provide a common standard.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that SI units are a common or universal standard used around the world.

rubric.why: Using standard units helps scientists communicate and compare measurements and results without confusion.
rubric.description: Gives a benefit of using standard units in science.
rubric.how: Award for giving a valid benefit, such as easier communication, comparison or avoiding confusion.

modelAnswer: S.I. units provide a common standard of measurement used by scientists throughout the world.
They make measurements and results easier to communicate and compare, and help avoid confusion.
